cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz saw this vision about Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1). God has just told His people to wash themselves clean and stop doing evil (Isaiah 1:16). Now Isaiah says, "See how the faithful city has become a harlot!"

cards.question: Isaiah says the city was once full of justice, with righteousness living inside her. Who does he say is in her now?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says the city's silver has become dross. That's like opening a cookie box you KNOW was full and finding nothing but crumbs staring back at you.

cards.question: Isaiah says the city's fine wine is now diluted with ___.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says the city's rulers are rebels and friends of THIEVES, baker. That's not a résumé line, that's a warning label.

cards.question: Isaiah says the rulers of the city all love something. What is it?
God told His people to defend the fatherless (Isaiah 1:17). Isaiah says the city's rulers defend the fatherless.

cards.text: And the plea of the widow never even comes before them. Therefore, the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, makes a declaration.

cards.question: The Lord GOD of Hosts says He will be relieved of His foes. What does He say He'll do to His enemies?

cards.text: Then the Lord says He will turn His hand against the city and thoroughly purge its dross. If I heard the first half of that, I'd dive face-first into the chocolate chips, gold base and all, but friend, keep listening.

cards.question: The Lord says He will remove only some of the city's impurities and leave the rest.
The Lord says He will restore the city's judges as at first and its counselors as at the beginning.
The Lord says that after He restores the judges and counselors, the city will still be known as a harlot.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says Zion, another name for Jerusalem, will be redeemed with justice. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so when I hear "redeemed," I take that word personally.

cards.question: Isaiah says some of Zion's people will be redeemed with righteousness. Who are they?
Isaiah says rebels and those who forsake the LORD will be redeemed right along with Zion's repentant ones.

cards.text: Instead, Isaiah says rebels and sinners will be shattered together, and those who forsake the LORD will perish. Then he says, "Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen."

cards.question: Isaiah tells the people who delighted in the sacred oaks that they will become like an oak whose leaves are ___, like a garden without water.

cards.text: Last picture. Isaiah says the strong man will become tinder and his work will be a spark, and both will burn together.

cards.question: When the strong man and his work burn together, someone will be there to put out the flames.
